newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia, Libya finalise gas pipeline joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia, Libya finalise gas pipeline joint venture.

text.p: Tunisia and Libya have agreed to set up a joint venture to develop a gas pipeline project by which Tripoli would supply southern Tunisia with gas, energy sources said on Friday.

Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi had announced at the end of a visit to Tunisia last November that the two nieghbouring countries agreed to establish the gas pipeline which, he said, would be built by Libya.

Energy officials said Tunisian Industry Minister Slaheddine Bouguerra and Libyan Energy Minister Mohamed Salem al-Badri had decided to set up the joint venture at talks earlier this week in the Tunisian island of Djerba.
The two ministers decided to speed up the development of the project and asked technicians to finish studies by the end of June.
The pipeline would run from the Mellita area, west of the Libyan coastal city of Sabratha, to the southern Tunisian city and industrial zone of Gabes.
The two ministers also agreed on the financing scheme of a project for the connexion between the Libyan and Tunisian power grids, the sources said.
